reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 shows the W-Ta-Ti-V-Cr system forms multiple phases with precipitates, not a single-phase BCC solid solution, and E2 studies different alloys (HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr) at lower temperatures (298–573 K) without comparing to pure tungsten or measuring toughness, so the claimed lattice distortion, diffusion, and toughness mechanisms are unsupported.
premises: Equimolar WTaTiVZr forms a single-phase BCC solid solution without significant secondary phases
Multi-element composition creates severe lattice distortions that slow atomic diffusion
Severe lattice distortions enhance dislocation interaction and entanglement
Sluggish diffusion and lattice strain increase activation energy for dislocation motion
Higher activation energy and dislocation entanglement produce greater plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten
